scoring_justification: Full recompute of the free energy derivative from the agent's evidence files requires implementing the complete pair-potential model, lattice sum, and Hildebrand equation of state, which is impractical for the verifier. Instead, we rely on the paper-reported gold values with tolerances that absorb implementation variation.

hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper text: experimental solubility limit at T=600 K is x=0.20 (used as calibration input for parameter p).
hidden_assets.generation_method: read from the paper's description of the phase diagram and the calibration condition.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The value is the experimental fact used by the paper itself; a correct reproduction must match it within tolerance.

hidden_assets.source_provenance: Fig. 6 in the paper: effective valence number z at x=0.2 and T=600 K is approximately 0.86.
hidden_assets.generation_method: read from the figure's data point; the reference solution hardcodes this value.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: It is the paper's headline result; the verifier compares the agent's computed z to this physically determined reference.

schema.description: a single floating-point number representing the mole fraction of AgBr in α-AgI at which ∂F/∂x=0 at T=600 K

outputs.description: Solubility limit composition x (mole fraction) at T=600 K

schema.description: a single floating-point number representing the effective valence (ionicity) of silver ions at x=0.2 AgBr and T=600 K

outputs.description: Effective valence number z at x=0.2, T=600 K (dimensionless)

output_contract.notes: Both outputs are single numbers written as plain text. The solubility limit is expected to be very close to the experimental input used for calibration (0.20) as a consistency check; the effective valence is the main reproduced quantity.
